advances: The row-level direction has a central captured-pair premise. Its existence alone does not enforce a feasible stochastic matrix perturbation.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: The joint cap derivative lemma and threshold stationarity give $\nabla P(c)=dP(c)b$, so $v$ is tangent to $b\cdot c=0$. The centroid lies on the cut and, because the cut is proper, is interior to the simplex. Thus the cap is stationary among oriented planes through the point with barycentrics $b$. Apply the positive-pair calculation in accepted fact 27d3881f8bfc290c to this stationary cap: its exact pair vector is $v$, the required two barycentric coordinates are at most $1/d$, and the chosen vertices are strictly captured. That calculation gives $v^\mathsf{T}Hv<0$, including the equal-margin limit and other zero margins. The optimized-capacity square formula with $s=\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}Hv/(dP(c))$ cancels the threshold penalty and proves the conclusion. Together with the strictly negative common-shift quadratic value in that formula, this supplies both signs at such a row.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let a strictly positive row $x$ have a proper minimizing threshold for the uniform-simplex capacity $\phi_d$. Normalize its threshold to one, let $c=\mathbf 1-x$, and set $P(c)=\Pr(\sum_j c_jE_j\ge0)$ for independent unit exponentials, $H=\nabla^2P(c)$, and $b$ equal to the actual barycentric section centroid. Suppose $c_i,c_j>0$ at distinct indices with $b_i,b_j\le1/d$. Put
$$
v=d b_j e_i-d b_i e_j,\qquad
w=v+\frac{\mathbf 1^\mathsf{T}Hv}{dP(c)}\mathbf 1.
$$
Then $w^\mathsf{T}\nabla^2\phi_d(x)w=-P(c)^{-1/d}v^\mathsf{T}Hv/(dP(c))>0$. Other margins may be zero and the two captured heights may coincide.
title: Positive capacity curvature from a corrected central pair
